content.subject: Basic Electrical Engineering
content.topic: Resistance vs Impedance: DC and AC Circuits
content.hook: Wires can fight back in two completely different ways depending on which way current flows.
content.question: Why does AC call opposition impedance instead of resistance?
content.outro: Thanks for watching. Next time you see alternating current, you will know exactly why impedance rules the circuit.

script.narration: Hi, ready for an explainer? here we go!

doodle.subject: mascot
doodle.action: waves warmly with a welcoming grin to begin the lesson
doodle.gag: light bulb glowing with little radiant eyelashes

script.narration: Every electric circuit pushes back against moving electric charges. But why do we say resistance in direct current circuits and impedance in alternating current circuits?

doodle.subject: mascot
doodle.action: rubs chin thoughtfully while looking back and forth between two power sources
doodle.gag: wall socket looks surprised with two wide round slot eyes

script.narration: When charges march in a single steady direction, we call it direct current. Batteries deliver this steady push, keeping electrons flowing in one continuous unbroken loop.
Alternating current behaves completely differently. Instead of marching ahead, wall outlets shake electrons back and forth fifty or sixty times every single second without stopping.

doodle.subject: illustration
doodle.action: a row of circular charge particles vibrating rapidly back and forth inside a wire section
doodle.gag: one charge particle wearing tiny running shoes skidding to a halt

script.narration: Think of resistance like walking through deep friction mud. Every single step collides with obstacles, turning your forward energy straight into wasted thermal heat.

doodle.subject: illustration
doodle.action: a pair of heavy boots trudging through thick sticky mud with heat ripples rising upward
doodle.gag: a tiny wilted flower drooping in the mud

script.narration: Inside a classic resistor, moving charges constantly smash into metal atoms. This pure collisions friction simply burns up electric voltage regardless of current flow direction.
Because direct current never changes direction, resistors are the only components offering permanent steady opposition. That simple opposition is what we formally call resistance.

doodle.subject: mascot
doodle.action: gestures toward a tidy direct-current loop containing a battery and a single resistor

script.narration: Yet alternating current introduces a brand new kind of opposition called reactance. Total opposition becomes impedance, combining ordinary resistive friction with reactive timing pushback.

doodle.subject: illustration
doodle.action: a flowing wavy current path hitting a barrier made of a rough brick block and a coiled metal spring
doodle.props: wavy current line, brick block, spring
doodle.gag: spring squashed completely flat against the brick

script.narration: Impedance is the grand total hurdle that an alternating circuit presents. It bundles ordinary resistance together with the stubborn magnetic and electric fields of other components.
To understand where this new reactance comes from, look at two everyday parts: inductors and capacitors. Both behave radically differently in DC compared to AC.

doodle.subject: mascot
doodle.action: points outward comparing a coiled wire inductor side by side with a two-plate capacitor

script.narration: An inductor is simply a wire coiled in loops. When electric current flows through these tight turns, it builds an invisible magnetic field around itself.
In a direct current circuit, an inductor acts like a stubborn flywheel. It momentarily delays initial turn on, but then settles into an easy passage.

doodle.subject: illustration
doodle.action: a steady straight arrow gliding effortlessly through a coiled wire looped around a flywheel
doodle.gag: a tiny snail cruising easily along the smooth wire path

script.narration: Steady DC electrons glide smoothly through the inductor copper wire. Once the magnetic field stabilizes, the coil turns into an ordinary path with zero special opposition.
Now connect alternating current to that same inductor. The current constantly changes direction, forcing the magnetic field to expand and collapse without a moment of peace.

doodle.subject: mascot
doodle.action: looks wide-eyed at an inductor coil surrounded by rapid pulsating concentric field rings
doodle.gag: field loops puffed up like an overinflated balloon ready to burst

script.narration: Every rapid reversal produces a counter voltage that chokes changing current. The incoming wave is blocked repeatedly, creating massive inductive reactance against high frequency alternating current.
Now look at a capacitor, which consists of two parallel metal plates separated by an insulator gap. Air or plastic prevents electrons from crossing directly across.
Feed direct current into this capacitor. Electrons rush onto one plate until it fills up completely, whereupon the open barrier stops all further current completely dead.
So in a DC circuit, a capacitor behaves like an open broken switch. Its resistance to steady current is essentially infinite once its plates are fully charged.

doodle.subject: illustration
doodle.action: two parallel plates blocking a circuit like an open drawbridge with halted charges piled up
doodle.gag: a tiny striped railway crossing barrier arm lowered across the wire gap

script.narration: Yet alternating current tricks the capacitor entirely. Electrons pour in to charge one side, quickly drain away as polarity flips, and fill the other side instead.

doodle.subject: illustration
doodle.action: charges sloshing smoothly into one capacitor plate, emptying out, and filling the opposite plate
doodle.gag: charges look like water tilting inside two balanced buckets

script.narration: No electron ever jumps the insulating gap between plates. But because charges slosh continuously in the outside connecting wires, alternating current flows through with minimal opposition.

doodle.subject: mascot
doodle.action: snaps fingers in sudden realization beside a capacitor with continuous external wire motion

script.narration: Notice the beautiful mirror symmetry between them. Inductors love steady direct current but choke alternating current, while capacitors block DC entirely and happily conduct alternating signals.

doodle.subject: illustration
doodle.action: a split mirror comparison showing a coil easily passing DC while choking AC, beside a capacitor doing the exact opposite
doodle.props: inductor coil, capacitor, straight and wavy arrows
doodle.gag: coil smiling at straight arrow and frowning at wavy arrow

script.narration: Resistance wastes energy as heat while reactance merely stores and releases energy in fields. When both forces work together in AC, we need the unified term impedance.

doodle.subject: mascot
doodle.action: balances hands apart showing rising heat waves beside an expanding energy storage bubble
doodle.gag: resistor wearing tiny sweat drops from working hard

script.narration: Engineers measure both resistance and impedance in ohms. But impedance reminds us that frequency, magnetic pushback, and electrostatic storage all dictate how much current actually flows.

doodle.subject: mascot
doodle.action: palms up playfully comparing two identical round meter dials with matching needle angles

script.narration: Direct current only faces simple resistance from collisions. Alternating current encounters impedance, which adds the magnetic resistance of inductors and electrostatic behavior of capacitors into total opposition.

doodle.subject: illustration
doodle.action: a straight easy single-speed track beside a wavy obstacle course featuring a resistor hill, coil loop, and plate gap
doodle.props: straight track, obstacle course track, coil, capacitor
doodle.gag: wavy course resembles a looping wooden roller coaster

script.narration: Here are the formulas behind this one. Save it for your revision.
Next time you look at a power supply or audio speaker, remember that alternating current is a dance, and impedance choreographs every single move.

doodle.subject: mascot
doodle.action: raises one hand in victory beneath a sweeping alternating wave curving through the air
doodle.gag: sine wave accented with tiny dancing musical notes

seo.description: Master Resistance vs Impedance in DC and AC circuits for State AE and JE Electrical exams. This video explains why direct current encounters pure resistance while alternating current faces the combined opposition of impedance. Learn how inductors and capacitors react differently across DC and AC sources, creating inductive and capacitive reactance. - Difference between direct current and alternating current - Why DC circuits only experience resistance - Role of inductors and capacitors in AC circuits - How reactance combines with resistance to form impedance - Why impedance and resistance are both measured in ohms. Subscribe for more State AE and JE Electrical concept lessons. #ResistanceVsImpedance #BasicElectricalEngineering #StateJEElectrical #ACCircuits
